newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Democrats decline S.African government role.
newsitem.headline: Democrats decline S.African government role.

text.p: South African President Nelson Mandela's overtures to try and widen his government's coalition stumbled on Sunday when the small Democratic Party declined an offer to join.
"The conditions proposed would have made it impossible for the party to play a strategic role as an opposition party," a spokeswoman for the mainly white liberal party said.
Democratic Party (DP) leader Tony Leon talked with Mandela earlier this year and was, like the leader of the leftist Pan Africanist Congress (PAC), reportedly offered a cabinet post.

The dilemma for the two small parties was that any role in government, while boosting their national profile ahead of the 1999 elections, could compromise them and blur public perception of how they differed from Mandela's African National Congress.
The PAC said in January it had accepted in principle a role in government, but appears since then to have got cold feet.
The National Party of South Africa's last white president F.W. de Klerk pulled out of the 1994 unity government in June, saying it would be better off as a vociferous opposition force.
Only the Zulu-based Inkatha Freedom Party of Mangosuthu Buthelezi is still in the coalition with ANC. Mandela, who champions consensus and racial reconciliation, is keen to broaden his government.
